Germans rent, Romanians own, Finns move out at 21 and Croatians at 31. Three maps of how Europe lives at home.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Who owns their home? Romania 94%, Slovakia 93%, Hungary 92%, Croatia 91%, Poland 87%. At the other end: Switzerland 42%, Germany 47%, Austria 54%. Data: Eurostat (EU-SILC 2024), share of people living in owner-occupied homes.
2/ Note the split: most of the former Eastern Bloc sits above 85%, while some of the richest economies in the west and centre of the continent have the most renters.

3/ When do young people leave their parents? Finland 21.4, Denmark 21.7, Sweden 21.9. Croatia 31.3, Slovakia 30.9, Greece 30.7, Italy 30.1, Spain 30.0. On average a young Finn moves out almost ten years earlier than a young Croatian. Data: Eurostat (2024).

4/ Who is drowning in housing costs? Share of people spending 40%+ of disposable income on housing: Greece 28.9%, Norway 15.4%, Switzerland 15.3%, Denmark 14.6%, Germany 12.0%. Lowest: Albania 2.3%, Croatia 3.7%. Data: Eurostat (EU-SILC 2024).
5/ Greece stands out on two maps at once: young Greeks leave home at 30.7 on average, and almost 3 in 10 people spend at least 40% of their income on housing.
Own or rent: which do you think is the better deal where you live? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
